रक्ताङ्ग: Raktāṅga m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya; described as ‘fast as wind’ (वातवेग), ‘having excess of poison’ (विषोल्बण) 1. 52. 16, 13, 1.
रभेणक: Rabheṇaka m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the family of Takṣaka, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacri-fice of Janamejaya 1. 52. 7, 9.
राक्षस: Rākṣasa m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya; described as ‘fast as wind’ (वातवेग), ‘having excess of poison’ (विषोल्बण) 1. 52. 16, 13, 1.

Rākṣasa adj.: of the व्यूह (arrange-ment of the army) known to the Rakṣases. Bhīṣma knew these and is said to have used them on different days along with those known to the Asuras and the Piśācas 6. 104. 16.
राजधर्मन्: Rājadharman m.: A mythical crane (बक 12. 167. 10, 15), also called Kāśyapa and Naḍījaṅgha. A. Birth: Son of Dākṣāyaṇī (referred to as देवकन्या 12. 163. 19) and Kaśyapa 12. 164. 2. B. Residence (भवन 12. 163. 17; निलय 12. 163. 23; निवेशन 12. 166. 10; गृह 12. 166. 6; आलय 12. 167. 14): Under a big न्यग्रोध tree, on a space covered with golden sand, in a forest near the ocean; the place was frequented by the यक्षस् and किन्नरस्; the residence looked like the seat of Pitāmaha (पितामहसदोपमम्) 12. 163. 6-7; 11-13. C. Description: Of pure soul (विशुद्धात्मन् 12. 166. 10), noble-minded (महात्मन् 12. 165. 7; 12. 167. 15), magnanimous (महामनस् 12. 164. 6), of great understanding (महामति 12. 164. 10), intelligent (धीमन्त् 12. 165. 27), eloquent (वाग्मिन् 12. 164. 9). D. Status: King of the cranes (बकराज् 12. 164. 9; बकराज 12. 166. 2; 12. 167. 2, 5; बकपति 12. 165. 31; 12. 167. 1, 8; बकाधिप 12. 167. 5, 13, 14; बकेन्द्र 12. 167. 8); best among the birds or king of the birds (खगोत्तम 12. 165. 26; खगेन्द्र 12. 166. 1); Brahma-deva when angered, however, called him ‘wicked-minded’ (दुष्टात्मन्) and ‘worst among the cranes’ (बकाधम) 12. 167. 9. E. Visits to Brahmaloka: It was Rājadharman's practice to go to Brahma-loka during the first twilight to pay homage to god Brahmadeva 12. 166. 6; on his return journey from Brahmaloka Rājadharman used to meet his friend the Rākṣaka king Virūpākṣa every day 12. 166. 6. F. Encounter with the Brāhmaṇa Gautama: Once when Rājadharman returned from Brahmaloka in the evening he met Gautama who happened to be at his residence 12. 163. 17; Rājadharman received him as his guest with due rites and offered him a seat of शाल flowers; he also gave him big fishes from Ganges and fire (for his protec-tion during the night); he fanned Gautama with his wings to remove his fatigue and then asked Gautama his गोत्र; Gautama told him only his name and that he was a Brāhmaṇa but nothing else (सो ऽब्रवीद् गौतमो ऽस्मीति ब्राह्म नान्यद् उदाहरत् 12. 164. 7); Rājadharman offered his guest a bed of leaves, rich in fragrance and strewn with fragrant, heavenly flowers; when Rāja-dharman (Kāśyapa) asked him the reason of his arrival, Gautama told him that since he was poor he wanted to go on sea in search of wealth; Rājadharman (Kāśyapa) told Gautama that he need have no anxiety for wealth, since according to Bṛhaspati, there were four means of acquiring wealth, viz. inheritance, luck, effort, and friend (चतुर्-विधा ह्य् अर्थगतिर् बृहस्पतिमतं यथा । पारंपर्यं तथा दैवं कर्म मित्रम् इति प्रभो 12. 164. 12); Rājadharman, as Gautama's friend, would help him to acquire wealth; in the morning he asked Gautama to go a distance of three योजनस् along a par-ticular way where, in the city Meruvraja, lived Rājadharman's friend Virūpākṣa the chief of the Rākṣasas (राक्षसाधिपति); Rājadharman was to Virūpākṣa his brother, relative and a dear friend; Rājadharman always trusted Virūpākṣa (स (i. e. Rāja-dharman) हि माम् आश्रितः सदा) 12. 165. 8; hence when Gautama met Virūpākṣa he was prepared to give Gautama all that he desired 12. 163. 22-23; 12. 164. 3-16; when Gau-tama returned from Virūpākṣa carrying with him heavy load of gold to Rājadharman's residence under the न्यग्रोध tree, the latter welcomed Gautama and tried to remove his fatigue by fanning him with wings; he offered Gautama food 12. 165. 27; Gautama thought of returning home but since he had nothing to eat on way the ungrateful Gautama decided to kill Rāja-dharman who was a heap of flesh 12. 165. 31; Rājadharman had kept fire burning with flames for the protection of Gautama at night, and he slept by the side of Gautama fully trusting him (विश्वस्त); Gautama killed Rājadharman with a fire-brand; he dressed the bird by removing his wings and hair (स तं विपक्षरोमाणं कृत्वा 12. 166. 4) and roasted him on fire; then taking the gold and meat with him Gautama started off 12. 166. 1-4; when a couple of days passed without Rājadharman's going to meet Virūpākṣa on his way home from the Brahmaloka, Virūpākṣa was worried about Rājadharman's safety; he suspected that Gautama, devoid of virtues as he was, might have killed Rājadharman; he therefore asked his son to visit Rājadharman's residence and find out whether he was alive; Virū-pākṣa's son saw near the न्यग्रोध tree only a skeleton of Rājadharman; he and his as-sociates pursued Gautama, captured him, and returned to Virūpākṣa with the body of Rāja-dharman which was without wings, bones and feet (°शरीरं च पक्षास्थिचरणोज्झितम् 12. 166. 13) 12. 166. 5-14; Virūpākṣa lame-nted over the loss of his friend and prepared a funeral pyre decorated with jewels, and spread over with perfumes and many pieces of cloth; after kindling the pyre of Rājadharman, Virūpākṣa performed the prescribed funeral rites; at that time divine Surabhi, daughter of Dakṣa, happened to stand above the pyre (in the sky); the foam from her mouth, mixed with milk, fell down on the burning pyre; Rājadharman came back to life and met Virūpākṣa; at that time Indra arrived on the scene and was glad that Rājadharman was alive (दिष्ट्यायं जीवतीत्य् उत 12. 167. 6); Indra told them an old incident (पुरा-तनम् 12. 167. 7): on a certain occasion, Rājadharman had failed to present himself in the assembly (सदस्) of Brahmadeva; the enraged god cursed Rājadharman to die soon (तस्माद् वधं स दुष्टात्मा नचिरात् समवाप्स्यति 12. 167. 9 [न चिरात् seems to contradict पुरातनम्]); hence Rājadharman was killed by Gautama, but was again revived by Brahman by sprinkling nectar 12. 167. 1-10; since Indra was favourably dis-posed to Rājadharman he was requested by Rājadharman to bring Gautama back to life; Indra revived Gautama and gave him to Rājadharman; delighted Rājadharman em-braced Gautama who had with him all kinds of vessels full of gold (सभाण्डोपस्करम् 12. 167. 13); Rājadharman then took leave of Gautama and returned home 12. 167. 11-14; Rājadharman, as usual, visited the above of Brahmadeva and was received with guest worship 12. 167. 15; this narrative of Rāja-dharman and Gautama is called आख्यान 12. 167. 18. [See Nāḍījaṅgha]
रेणुक: Reṇuka m.: A mythical bird (पक्षिन्). He fought with Garuḍa when the latter was on his expedition to fetch अमृत; Garuḍa tore him apart with his wings, nails and beak 1. 28. 18 (According to Nī. the name of a Yakṣa, cf. his remark on 1. 32. 18 Bom. Ed.).
रक्षसाम्: Rakṣasām astrāṇi nt. pl.: Missiles special to Rakṣases. Arjuna was to learn these after reaching the residence of Indra 3. 164. 29-30.
रुद्राणाम्: Rudrāṇām astrāṇi nt. pl.: Missiles special to the Rudras. When Arjuna reached Indra's residence, the Rudras, along with the other group-gods, agreed to give their missiles to him 3. 164. 49-50; they figure in a bad omen: when Garuḍa flew up from a mountain top to fetch Soma from the heaven, there occurred bad omens for the gods, one of them being that the missile (प्रहरणम्) of the Rudras clashed with those of the Vasus, the Ādityas, the Sādhyas, the Maruts and the other hosts of gods (ये चान्ये देवतागणाः); such a thing had never happened before 1. 26. 29-30.
रुद्रास्त्र: Rudrāstra, Raudra astra nt.: Name of a missile, special to Rudra (Śiva). A. Description: Heavenly (दिव्य) 12. 5. 13-14; great (महास्त्र) 3. 170. 38; fierce (घोर) 3. 170. 40; 7. 53. 43; eternal (सनातन) 3. 170. 40; destroyer of all ene-mies (सर्वामित्रविनाशन) 3. 170. 38; no other weapon superior to it (अनुत्तम) 8. 66. 57. B. Identified with the Pāśupata (and the Brahmaśiras ?): When Arjuna prayed to Śiva to give him the divine missiles, he agreed to Arjuna's request and told him that his Raudra missile would wait on him; he then gave him his Pāśupata 3. 163. 47-48; Brahma-śiras missile, which Arjuna received from Rudra, also called Raudra (or adj. ‘fierce’ of Brahmaśiras (?)) 3. 41. 8. C. Known to Arjuna: Arjuna's collection of missiles (अस्त्रग्राम 5. 166. 32) included Raudra astra 3. 89. 10-11; Arjuna had received it from Rudra 7. 53. 43; 12. 5. 13-14, and he wanted to use it against the Kauravas at the time of the cattle-raid 4. 56. 14. D. Mode of use: At the time of using it (against Karṇa), Arjuna recited the मन्त्रस् (अनु-मन्त्र्य) on the arrow on which he employed it 8. 66. 58; at the time of charging his arrow with the missile (to release it against the Pauloma and the Kālakeya demons) Arjuna bowed down to Rudra (रुद्राय प्रणतो रणे) and wished well to the crea-tures (स्वस्ति भूतेभ्यः); he bowed down to Śarva (Rudra) again when he actually released the missile from the bow (नमस्कृत्वा त्रिनेत्राय शर्वायामिततेजसे) 3. 170. 38, 41. E. Uses: 1. In the epic war: (i) Arjuna wanted to employ it on a heavenly arrow, resembling fire or snake's poison and which was hard like a stone, and release it against Kaṛṇa 8. 66. 58-59; there is no mention of Arjuna having released it, but it seems that he warded off Karṇa's Brahmāstra with it (not named; तद् अस्त्रम् अस्त्रेणावार्य प्रज-हारास्य पाण्डवः) 8. 67. 8; (ii) Aśva-tthāman killed the followers of Dhṛṣṭadyumna who surrounded him after he killed Dhṛṣṭa-dyumna at night in the camp of the Pāṇḍavas 10. 8. 31-32; 2. Outside the epic war: (i) Arjuna used it to burn with its fire the Nivātakavaca demons 5. 136. 7; (ii) Arjuna used it to kill the Pauloma and the Kālakeya demons; Arjuna first used all his other missiles without being able to defeat the demons, but was himself oppressed by them; at that time he was afraid; he bowed to Rudra and employed the great Raudra missile on his arrow (महा-स्त्रं समयोजयम्); he then saw a man having three heads, nine eyes, three mouths, six hands, burning, his hair bright like the sun or fire, his head covered with big snakes (ततो ऽपश्यं त्रिशिरसं पुरुषं नवलोच-नम् । त्रिमुखं षड्भुजं दीप्तम् अर्क-ज्वलनमूर्धजम् ॥ लेलिहानैर् महानागैः कृतशीर्षम्) 3. 170. 38-39; when the missile was next actually released (मुक्तमात्रे ततस् तस्मिन्) thousands of different shapes—wild animals like lions, tigers, bears, buffalos, as also snakes, cows, elephants, सृमरस्, शरभस्, bulls, boars, wild cats, शालावृकस्, ghosts, भुरुण्डस्, vultures, eagles, crocodiles, Piśācas, Yakṣas, demons, Guhyakas, Nairṛtas, big fishes having mouths of elephants, owls, hosts of fishes and tortoises, shapes holding different weapons and swords, Yātudhānas holding गदा and मुद्गर, and many others—came out from the missile and filled the space; the demons were killed by many shapes having three heads, four tusks, four mouths, four hands, as also by the arrows of Arjuna which shone like the sun and the fire, which were brilliant like the Vajra and lightning, and hard like rocks; when the demons were killed by the Raudrāstra, Arjuna bowed down to Tripuraghna (Śiva) once again 3. 170. 42-51.
रौद्र: Raudra m.: Name of a मुथूर्त। Relationship with events: (1) Epic: (a) Arjuna warned Bhīma during his noctu-ral fight with Hiḍimba that with the advent of the Raudra मुहूर्त the Rākṣasas grew stronger (रौद्रे मुहूर्ते रक्षांसि प्रब-लानि भवन्ति च) 1. 142. 22; (b) On the fourteenth day of the war Arjuna appeared on the scene under the Raudra मुहूर्त when the two armies were about to clash (रौद्रे मुहूर्ते संप्राप्ते सव्यसाची व्यदृश्यत) 7. 64. 3; (रौद्र मुहूर्त very probably ‘terrible hour’ 8. 68. 35); (2) Mytho-logical: During his conversation with Deva-senā, Indra observed that the Raudra मुहूर्त had commenced on a new-moon day (अमा-वास्यां संप्रवृत्तं मुहूर्तं रौद्रम् एव च) 3. 213. 27; (धर्मगतं रौद्रम् ? 3. 213. 30).

Raudra m. (pl.): Name of a people (?) A. Location: Near the southern ocean (see the Epic event). B. Epic event: When Arjuna, accompanying the Aśva-medha horse, reached the southern ocean he had to fight with Raudras and Māhiṣakas along with others (प्रययौ भूयो दक्षि-णं सलिलार्णवम् ॥ तत्रापि … रौद्रैर् माहिषकैर् अपि । … युद्धम् आसीत् किरीटि-नः ॥ ) 14. 84. 10-11 (Is Raudra a proper name, or does it mean ‘fierce’ and qualify Māhiṣakas ?).
रथातिरथसङ्ख्या: Rathātirathasaṃkhyā f.: Name of the 57th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 53, 33, 70. Referred to as ‘counting of the Rathas and Atirathas’ (रथातिरथसंख्यानम्) in the listing of the contents of the Udyoga-parvan 1. 2. 150; during the war the Kaurava army remembered Karṇa (who was absent from the battle-field for the first ten days of the war) at the fall of Bhīṣma and recollected that in the incident of counting the Rathas and the Atirathas Bhīṣma had rated Karaṇa as Ardharatha although he was twice as good as that kind of a warrior (संख्यातो ऽर्धरथः कर्णो द्विगुणः सन् नरषभ) 7. 1. 33-35; referred to in the summary of the events made by Dhṛtarāṣṭra for Saṃjaya 1. 1. 122; related to the अध्यायस् 5. 161-169.
रथातिरथसंख्या: Rathātirathasaṃkhyā f.: Name of the 57th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 53, 33, 70. Referred to as ‘counting of the Rathas and Atirathas’ (रथातिरथसंख्यानम्) in the listing of the contents of the Udyoga-parvan 1. 2. 150; during the war the Kaurava army remembered Karṇa (who was absent from the battle-field for the first ten days of the war) at the fall of Bhīṣma and recollected that in the incident of counting the Rathas and the Atirathas Bhīṣma had rated Karaṇa as Ardharatha although he was twice as good as that kind of a warrior (संख्यातो ऽर्धरथः कर्णो द्विगुणः सन् नरषभ) 7. 1. 33-35; referred to in the summary of the events made by Dhṛtarāṣṭra for Saṃjaya 1. 1. 122; related to the अध्यायस् 5. 161-169.
राजधर्म: Rājadharma m.: Name of the 86th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha (राजधर्-मानुकीरतनम्) 1. 2. 64, 33, 70. Referred to in the listing of the contents of the Śāntiparvan as describing the duties which must be understood by kings who wish to know the correct policy (राजभिर् वेदि-तव्या ये सम्यङ्नयबुभुत्सुभिः) 1. 2. 197; related to the अध्यायस् 12. 1-128.
राजसूयिक: Rājasūyika nt.: Name of the 24th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha; it occurs after the Digvijaya parvan 1. 2. 40, 33, 70. Referred to in the listing of the contents of the Sabhāparvan as राजसूये ऽर्घसं-वादे 1. 2. 99; mentioned in the summary of the events made by Sūta Ugraśravas for the sages assembled at the सत्र of Śaunaka 1. 1. 84-85, and in the summary of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra made for Saṃjaya 1. 1. 99; related to the अध्यायस् 2. 30-32.
राज्यलम्भ: Rājyalambha m.: Name of the 15th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 37, 33, 70. Described in the listing of the contents of the Ādiparvan as: “Pāṇḍavas starting their life in the Khāṇḍavaprastha and ruling over half the kingdom; entering into an agree-ment regarding Draupādī at the instance of Nārada (नारदस्याज्ञाया चैव द्रौपद्याः समयक्रिया); the narration of the उपा-ख्यान related to Sunda and Upasunda” 1. 2. 89-90; referred to in the summary of the events made by Vaiśaṃpāyana for Jana-mejaya 1. 55. 23-27; related to the अध्याय 1. 199.
रामचरित: Rāmacarita nt.: Name of an आख्यान (?) (आख्याते रामचरिते) composed by Bhārgava 12. 57. 40. Bhīṣma while discoursing on the duties of a king to Yudhiṣṭhira cities a श्लोक sung in the bygone days by Bhārgava in the Rāmacarita (श्लोकश् चायं पुरा गीत्ō भार्-गवेण महात्मना । आख्याते रामचरिते॑) 12. 57. 40; according to this श्लोक one should first seek a king and next a wife and riches; in the absence of a king, people can have neither wife nor riches (राजानं प्रथमं विन्देत् ततो भार्यां ततो ध-नम् । राजन्य् असलि लोकस्य कुतो भार्या कुतो धनम् ॥ ) 12. 57. 41.
रामायण: Rāmāyaṇa1 nt.: Name of an उपा-ख्यान। It is narrated in great details (बाहु-विस्तरम्); listed in the contents of the Āraṇyakaparvan 1. 2. 126; related to the अध्यायस् 3. 258-276.
Rāmāyaṇa2 nt.: Name of the epic. Referred to by Bhīma in his conversation with Hanūmān 3. 147. 11.
राका: Rākā f.: Name of the second Paurṇa-māsī when the full moon day extends to two days (cf. या पूर्वा पौर्णमासी सानुमतिर् योत्तरा सा राका Ait. Br. 32. 9; Nir. 11. 29). A. Description: Observing her vows strictly (सुव्रता) 8. 24. 74. B. Mytholo-gical events: (1) Rākā, personified, along with Anumatī and many others arrived at the river Sarasvatī to attend the investiture of Kumāra as the general of the gods 9. 44. 12, 16; (2) she served as one of the reins of the horses of Śiva's chariot when it was made ready for Śiva's fight with the Tripuras (कुहूं राकां च सुव्रताम् । योक्त्राणि चक्रुर् वाहानाम्) 8. 24. 74.
राहु: Rāhu m.: Name of a planet, also called Svarbhānu (6. 13. 39-40; 13. 17. 37). A. Description: Described as round (परिमण्डल) 6. 13. 40; fierce (तीव्र) 6. 3. 26; dark (श्याम) 6. 3. 15; blazing, (प्रज्वलित) 6. 3. 15; having smoke and fire सधूमः सहपावकः) 6. 3. 15; having copper-red crest (? ताम्र° °शिख) 6. 3. 24. B. Importance: Chief among the planets (ग्रहपतिर् वरः) 13. 17. 37; Rāhu, along with other planets, visits the सभा of Brah-man 2. 11. 20, 19; Rāhu, not directly named but probably referred to as Grahapati, finds place in the list of a thousand names of Śiva (केतुग्रहो ग्रहपतिर् वरः) 13. 17. 37 (however, Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 17. 38, interprets ग्रहः as राहुः: केतुश् च प्रसिद्-धः । चन्द्राक्रौ गृह्णातीति ग्रहो राहुः॑ ग्रहाणां पतिः [ग्रहपतिः] क्रूरत्वात् मंगलः); Rāhu finds place also in the Daivatavaṃśa 13. 151. 12. C. Measure-ment: Dhṛtarāṣṭra asked Saṃjaya to tell him complete extent (सर्वं (प्रमाणं)) of Rāhu, to which Saṃjaya agreed 6. 12. 3-4; according to the information of Saṃ-jaya his diameter (विष्कम्भ) was 12000 योजनस्, and his circumference (परिणाह) 36000 योजनस्; according to the learned Paurāṇikas his expanse (? विपुलत्व) was 6000 योजनस् (परिमण्डलो महाराज स्वर्-भानुः श्रूयते ग्रहः । योजनानां सह-स्राणि विष्कम्भो द्वादशास्य वै ॥ परिणा-हेन षट्त्रिंशद् विपुलत्वेन चानघ । षष्टिम् आहुः शतान्य् अस्य बुधाः पौरा-णिकास् तथा) 6. 13. 40-41 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 12. 41 interprets विपुलत्वेन as ततो ऽप्य् आधिक्येन, इदम् उत्तरान्वयि; in that case the circumference of Rāhu will be 36000 + 6000 = 42000 योजनस्; see also Editor's note on the stanza, Cr. Ed. Vol. 7, p. 765: “Saṃjaya is here relying upon his studies, and not upon the Eye Divine”); owing to its being larger in size than the sun and the moon, Rāhu covers them both at proper times (स राहुश् छादयत्य् एतौ (i. e. चन्द्रादित्यौ) यथाकालं महत्तया) 6. 13. 45. D. Omens: (1) Among the bad omens for the Kurus reported by Vyāsa to Dhṛtarāṣṭra one was related to Rāhu's swallowing the sun 6. 3. 11; this event is again referred to by Vyāsa as occurring at an improper time, i. e. on the thirteenth day of the month and in which Rāhu swa-llowed both Candra and Sūrya together; this meant destruction of the subjects 6. 3. 28-29 (for citation and Nī.'s commentary see Sūrya below); also cf. 14. 76. 15; 2. 71. 26; 9. 55. 10; the same was also noted by Karṇa and reported to Kṛṣṇa (राहुर् अर्कम् उपैष्यति) 5. 141. 10 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 5. 143. 11: अयं कर्तरीयोगः सोमवंश्यानां सूर्यवंश्यानां च राज्ञां क्षयकर इत्य् अर्थः); (reference to Rāhu implied in 6. 73. 10: प्रजासंहरणे सूर्यः क्रूरैर् इव महाग्रहैः (परिवृतः); (2) Among the omens noticed by Vyāsa there was also another according to which a black planet (= Rāhu) blazing, and full of smoke and fire had gone over to Jyeṣṭhā and remained there (श्यामो ग्रहः प्रज्वलितः सधू-मः सहपावकः । … ज्येष्ठाम् आक्रम्य तिष्ठति ॥ )) 6. 3. 15 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 3. 16 reads श्वेतो ग्रहः in place of श्यामो ग्रहः and explains it as Ketu: श्वेतो द्वितीय उपग्रहः केतुसंज्ञः); (3) Vyāsa had also noticed that the two Grahas (Rāhu and Ketu ?) having copper-red and ruddy crests (respy. ?) appear blazing in the sky and cover up the lustre of the seven sages (i. e. the constellation Ursa Major) (ग्रहौ ताम्रारुणशिखौ प्रज्वलन्ताव् इव स्थितौ । सप्तर् षीणाम् उदाराणां समवच्-छाद्य वै प्रभाम् ॥ ) 6. 3. 24; (4) Kṛṣṇa observed that the अमावास्या had already set in on the thirteenth day of the dark half of the month and that Rāhu had turned the fourteenth day into the fifteenth (which was looked upon as bad); he told the Yādavas that such an event had happened only once before at the time of the Bhārata war (a reference to 6. 3. 28-29 above) and that it had now occurred again to foretell the destruction of the Yādavas (त्रयो-दश्याम् अमावास्या तान् दृष्ट्वा प्राब्रवीद् इदम् ॥ चतुर्दशी पञ्चदशी कृतेयं राहुणा पुनः । तदा च भारते युद्धे प्राप्ता चाद्य क्षयाय नः ॥ ) 16. 3. 16-17 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 16. 2. 19, notices a hint of a solar eclipse in this statement: एवं सत्य् अग्रिम-पक्षे वृद्ध्या भाव्यं तन् न जातं प्रत्य् उत एका तिथिः क्षीणा तत्र ग्रहणं च जातम्). [See Dhūmaketu; for Rāhu, also see Section 1. 7]
रेवती: Revatī f.: Name of a constellation. A. Placement in the Śākadvīpa: In the Śākadvīpa, the constellation Revatī has been permanently stationed in the sky by an arrangement made by Pitāmaha (Brahman) (रेवती दिवि नक्षत्रम् (नित्यं) पितामह-कृतो विधिः ॥ ) 6. 12. 16 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 11. 18: रेवती ज्योतिर्मण्डलरूपेण दिवि विभ्रम्यमाणापि दिव्येन रूपेण अत्रापि वर्तते एवं विधिर् मर्यादा पितामहेन कृता). B. Auspicious constellation: Kṛṣṇa started for Hāstinapura on his peace mission under the constellation Revatī (रेवत्याम्) 5. 81. 7. C. Religious rites: (1) दान: Nārada told Devaki (13. 63. 2-4) that if one gave as a gift a milch cow together with a milk-pail made of white copper under Revatī, the cow waited upon the giver in his next life and fulfilled his wishes (कांस्यो-पदोहनां धेनुं रेवत्यां यो प्रयच्-छति । सा प्रेत्य कामान् आदाय दातारम् उप-तिष्ठति) 13. 63. 33; (2) श्राद्ध: Yama told Śaśabindu (13. 89. 1) that by offering a काम्य श्राद्ध under the Revatī one obtained wealth consisting of much silver (बहुरूप्यकृतं वित्तं विन्दते रेवतीं श्रितः) 13. 89. 14 (For Revatī also see Section 1. 7).
रोहिणी: Rohiṇī f. (sg., once pl. 12. 160. 80): Name of a constellation. A. Computation of time: Abhijit, youn-ger sister of Rohiṇī, vying with her and desiring for a higher rank went to forest to practise austerities; Indra was then confused in calculating time (due to the loss of a नक्षत्र) 3. 219. 8-9; hence Brahman ordained that time (काल) would commence with Dhaniṣṭhā, while formerly it commenced with Rchiṇī; this made good the loss of one नक्षत्र (रोहिण्याद्यो ऽभवत् पूर्वम् एवं संख्या समाभवत्) 3. 219. 10 (for full citation and Nī.'s commentary see Abhijit and Dhaniṣṭhā). B. Auspicious constellation: The Pāṇḍavas left for Vāraṇāvata on the eighth day of Phalguna and under the con-stellation Rohiṇī (रोहिण्याम्) 1. 133. 30. C. Religious rites: (1) दान: Nārada told Devakī (13. 63. 2-4) that in order to be free from debt (to the manes ?) one should, under the constellation Rohiṇī, feed the Brāhmaṇas with known kinds of meat, beans, cooked rice and clarified butter, and give them milk at the end of the meal (रोहिण्यां प्रथितैर् मांसैर् माषैर् अन्नेन सर्पिषा । पयो ऽनुपानं दातव्यम् आनृण्याय द्विजातये ॥ 13. 63. 6 (Nī. who reads प्रसृतैर् मार्गैर् मांसैर् explains मार्गैर् as मृगसंबन्धिभिः); (2) श्राद्ध: Yama told Śaśabindu (13. 89. 1) that one desirous of offspring should offer a श्राद्ध under Rohiṇī (रोहिण्याम्) 13. 89. 3. D. Rohiṇī and the असि: The sword which was created by Brahman as a weapon (12. 160. 42) had the Rohiṇī stars for their गोत्र (रोहिण्यो गोत्रम् अस्य (असेः)) 12. 160. 80. E. Omens: (1) Among the omens noticed by Vyāsa before the start of the war there was one according to which Śanaiścara was afflicting Rohiṇī (रोहिणीं पीडयन्न् एष स्थितो राजञ् शनैश्चरः) 6. 2. 32 (also cf. the next section F (3); also 5. 141. 7 ? see Prājāpatya2) (2) At the time of Karṇa's death, Bṛhaspati was afflicting Rohiṇī (बृहस्पती रोहिणीं संप्रपीड्य) 8. 68. 49. F. Similes: (1) Yudhiṣṭhira saw Gāndhārī surrounded by her daughters-in-law as is Rohiṇī by the stars (ताराभिर् इव रोहिणीम्) 2. 52. 27; (2) Lopāmudrā, sur-rounded by her hundred दासीस् and a hundred maidens, sat like Rohiṇī in the sky (रोहिणीव दिवि प्रभो) 3. 94. 24; (3) Rāvaṇa draw-ing near Sītā looked like the planet Śanaiś-cara when it approached Rohiṇī (ददृशे रोहिणीम् एत्य शनैश्चर इव ग्रहः) 3. 265. 6; (4) Śāntā waited on Ṛśyaśṛnga like Rohiṇī on Soma (रोहिणी सोमम् इवानु-कूला) 3. 113. 22; (5) Sudeva wondered when would Damayanti be united with Nala and reach the end of her hardship as Rohiṇī on meeting the moon (रोहिणी शशिनो यथा) 3. 65. 21. [See Prājāpatya2; for Rohiṇī also see Section 1. 7]
रथचित्रा: Rathacitrā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 25, 13 (for other details see Puṣpaveṇī).
रथस्था: Rathasthā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; people used its water for drinking 6. 10. 18, 13 (for other details see Puṣpaveṇī).
रथावर्त: Rathāvarta m.: Name of a sacred place. Situated to the right of the goddess at Dhūmāvatī (देव्यास् तु दक्षिणार्धेन र-थावर्तो नराधिप); if one mounts on the Rathāvarta with faith and with controlled senses he gets the highest condition by the favour of Mahādeva (तत्रारोहेत … श्रद्द-धानो जितेन्द्रियः । महादेवप्रसादाद् धि गच्छेत परमां गतिम् ॥ ) 3. 82. 21; circumambulating it one should proceed to the तीर्थ called Dhārā 3. 82. 22,
रमणी: Ramaṇī f.: Name of a तीर्थ। Listed in the Tīrthavaṃśa narrated by Aṅgiras 13. 26. 3; by bathing at Ramaṇī, while observing fast for a month, one gets the power of becoming invisible (?) (रम-ण्यां च उपस्पृश्य … एकमासं निराहारस् त्व् अन्तर्धानफलं लभेत्) 13. 26. 29 (Nī., however, on Bom. Ed. 13. 25. 30: अन्तर्धानफलं गन्धर्वादिभोगम्).
राजगृह: Rājagṛha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। One who is on a pilgrimage should visit Rājagṛha; by bathing in the hot springs (?) there one rejoices like Kākṣīvant; a pure person, by partaking of the food offered to the Yakṣiṇī there, is released by the favour of the Yakṣiṇī from the sin of killing an embryo (ततो राजगृहं गच्छेत् तीर्थसेवी  … । उपस्पृश्य तपोदेषु काक्षीवान् इव मो-दते ॥ यक्षिण्या नैत्यकं तत्र प्राश्नीत पुरुषः शुचीः । यक्षिण्यास् तु प्रसादेन मुच्यते भ्रूणहत्यया ॥ ) 3. 82. 89-90 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 84. 105: नित्यकं नैवेद्यं नैत्यकं च तद् एव).

Rājagṛha nt.: Name of a town. A. Location: The capital town of the Magadha country (गोप्ता मगधराष्ट्र-स्य दार्वो राजगृहे हतः) 1. 105. 10; (आसीद् राजगृहे राजा मागधानाम्) 1. 196. 17. B. Epic event: (1) Pāṇḍu killed Dārva the protector of the Magadha country, at Rājagṛha 1. 105. 10; he collected treasure, chariots and forces from the city before marching from there on Mithilā of the Videha country (ततः कोशं समादाय वाहनानि बलानि च । पाण्डुना मिथिलां गत्वा विदेहाः समरे जिताः) 1. 105. 11; (2) The sacrificial horse of the Pāṇḍavas reached Rājagṛha town while wandering at its own will (यदृच्छया समापेदे पुरं राजगृहं तदा) 14. 83. 2; Meghasaṃdhi marched out of the town (Rājagṛha) in a chariot, equipped with bows, arrows, and arm guards, to attack Arjuna (ततः पुरात् स निष्क्रम्य रथी धन्वी शरी तली) 14. 83. 2, 4. C. Past event: Formerly Ambuvīca was the king of the Magadha chieftains at Rājagṛha (श्रूयते हि पुरा कश्चिद् अम्बुवीच इति श्रुतः । आसीद् राजगृहे राजा मागधानां महीक्षिताम्) 1. 196. 17. [See Givīvraja; for Rājagṛha tīrtha see Vol. 1. 431-432]
रामक: Rāmaka m.: Name of a mountain. Situated near the island Tāmra (?) on the west coast not far from Śūrpāraka; Saha-deva conquered it in the expedition he under-took before the Rājasūya (द्वीपं ताम्रा-ह्वयं चैव पर्वतं रामकं तथा) 2. 28. 43, 46.
रामतीर्थ: Rāmatīrtha nt.: Name of different तीर्थस्, most of which are related to Rāma Jāmadagnya. (1) On the mountain Mahendra, re-sorted to by Jāmadagnya (hence so called); by bathing there one gets the fruit of a horse sacrifice (Vājimedha) 3. 83. 14; (2) Situ-ated at Śūrpāraka, resorted to by Jāma-dagnya (hence so called); by bathing there one gets much gold (विन्द्याद् बहु सुवर्ण-कम्) 3. 83. 40; (3) One described as auspicious (शुभ) and excellent तीर्थ (तीर्थवर) 9. 48. 6; Balarāma went to it from Indratīrtha 9. 48. 6; Rāma Bhārgava, after destroying the Kṣatriyas several times, offered at this तीर्थ a Vājapeya and a hundred horse sacrifices, and gave the whole earth as दक्षिणा 9. 48. 7-8; (4) Situated on the river Gomatī; by bathing there one gets the fruit of a horse sacrifice (Aśva-medha) and purifies his lineage (पुनाति च कुलं नरः) 3. 82. 66.
रामह्रद: Rāmahrada m. pl., (sg.): Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: Listed among the four places which form the boundaries of the Kurukṣetrasamantapañcaka (रामह्रदानाम्) 3. 81. 178; 9. 52. 20. B. Description: Holy (पुण्याः) 3. 81. 33; famous (विश्रु-ताः) 3. 81. 27. C. Holiness: (1) A pilgrim should visit them (रामह्रदान्) 3. 81. 22; by bathing at these lakes and by worshipping Rāma (Jāmadagnya) one who has observed chastity and practised auspicious vows obtains much gold (स्नात्वा ह्रदेषु रामस्य ब्रह्मचारी शुभव्रतः । रामम् अभ्यर्च्य राजेन्द्र लभेद् बहु सुवर्ण-कम् ॥ ) 3. 81. 33; (2) One should bathe in these lakes and satisfy manes; the manes, thus pleased, will grant him whatever unobtainable is desired by him and heaven for all times (ह्रदेष्व् एतेषु यः स्नात्वा पितॄन् संतर्-पयिष्यति । पितरस् तस्य वै प्रीता दास्यन्ति भुवि दुर्लभम् । ईप्सितं मनसः कामं स्वर्गलोकं च शाश्वतम् ॥ ) 3. 81. 31; (3) By bathing in this lake and by abstain-ing from food for twelve days one is freed of sin (रामह्रद उपस्पृश्य … । द्वादशा-हं निराहारः कल्मषाद् विप्रमुच्यते ॥ ) 13. 26. 44. D. History: Rāma (Bhār-gava), after extirpating the Kṣatriyas, founded five lakes and filled them with blood; he satisfied there his ancestors and grand-fathers (क्षत्रम् उत्साद्य वीर्येण ह्रदाः पञ्च निवेषिताः ॥ पूरयित्वा नरव्याघ्र रुधि-रेणेति नः श्रुतम् । पितरस् तर्पिताः सर्वे तथैव च पितामहाः) 3. 81. 22-23; Rāma requested the satisfied ancestors to turn the lakes of blood into तीर्थस्; this request was granted (ह्रदांश् च तीर्थभूता मे भवेयुः । … ह्रदाश् च तव तीर्थत्वं गमिष्यन्ति न संशयः) 3. 81. 27, 30. E. Epic event: (1) While visiting the तीर्थस् on the river Yamunā, Lomaśa pointed out these lakes to Yudhiṣṭhira (रामह्रदान्) 3. 129. 6; (2) Rāmahrada (रामह्रदे) was one of the places where Ambā bathed (आप्लावयत गात्राणि) and practised severe austerities to achieve her objective of killing Bhīṣma 5. 187. 27-28; (3) While proceed-ing to Kurukṣetra to meet Bhīṣma, Kṛṣṇa showed to Yudhiṣṭhira at some distance the five lakes of Rāma (अमी रामह्रदाः पञ्च दृश्यन्ते पार्थ दूरतः) 12. 48. 8. F. Past event: Rāma satisfied his ancestors with the blood of Kṣatriyas who were killed by him (येषु संतर्पयाम् आस पूर्वान् क्षत्रियशोणितैः); after rendering the earth devoid of Kṣatriyas twentyone times Rāma Jāmadagnya gave up this activity here (इहे-दानीं ततो राम कर्मणो विरराम ह) 12. 48. 8-9.
रुद्रकोटि: Rudrakoṭi1 f.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. History: Formerly a crore of devout sages sat down in order to see god (Śiva); they started for this place vying with one another to see god Śiva first; god Śiva with his divine power (योगम् आस्थाय) created a crore of Rudras in front of every one of them so that every one felt that he saw Rudra first (सृष्टा कोटिस् तु रुद्राणाम् ऋषीणाम् अग्रतः स्थिता । मया पूर्वतरं दृष्ट इति ते मेनिरे पृथक्) and did not entertain anger (with the thought that he was behind others in seeing Rudra) (तेषां मन्यु-प्रणाशार्थम् ऋषीणाम्); pleased Mahādeva granted them a boon so that their religious merit would increase (अद्यप्रभृति युष्मा-कं धर्मवृद्धिर् भविष्यति) 3. 80. 124-128. B. Holiness: A devout pilgrim should visit it; by bathing there, a pure person (नरः शुचिः) gets the fruit of an Aśvamedha and lifts up his family (कुलं चैव समुद्-धरेत्) 3. 80. 124, 129.
Rudrakoṭi2 f.: Name of a तीर्थ। Located at the holy place Saraka in a well and in lakes (सरके कुरुनन्दन । रुद्रकोटिस् तथा कूपे ह्रदेषु च मही-पते ॥ ) 3. 81. 63.
रुद्रावर्त: Rudrāvarta m.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated at the confluence of the rivers Gaṅgā and Sarasvatī; a pilgrim (तीर्थसेवी) should visit it; by bathing there one gets the fruit of an Aśvamedha and when he goes to heaven he is glorified there (स्वर्गलोके महीयते) 3. 82. 33-34.
रेणुकातीर्थ: Reṇukātīrtha nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated near the holy place called Kumārikāṇāṃ tīrtham (रेणुकायाश् च तत्-रैव तीर्थम्) 3. 80. 97-98; described as best (उत्तम) 3. 81. 139 and resorted to by gods (देवनिषेवित) 3. 80. 98; by bathing there a Brāhmaṇa becomes clean like the moon (विमलश् चन्द्रमा यथा) 3. 80. 98; by bathing there and by being engaged in the worship of manes and gods (पितृदेवार्-चने रतः) a man's soul is cleansed of all sins and he gets the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma 3. 81. 139.
रैवत: Raivata1, Raivataka1 m.: Name of a mountain. A. Location: In the west (प्रतीच्याम्); Raivata adorns the town Kuśasthalī (Dvā-rakā) 2. 13. 49. B. Description: Great mountain (महाशैल) 14. 58. 6; (महा-गिरि) 14. 58. 12; chief among mountains (गिरिमुख्य) 2. 13. 52; king of mountains (शैलराज्) 14. 58, 14; (शैलेन्द्र) 1. 212. 6; (पर्वतेन्द्र) 14. 58. 9; described at some length at the time of the festival of the mountain (वर्तमाने महाराज महे रैवतकस्य च): it was adorned with many variegated forms and it shone all around by the golden Kāśa grass (अलंकृतस् तु स गिरिर् नानारूपविचित्रितैः । बभौ रुक्म-मयैः काशैः सर्वतः); it was adorned with excellent golden garlands, flowers, cloth-pieces (वासोभिः) and by Kalpavṛkṣas (कल्प-वृक्षैश् च सर्वशः); it was adorned with golden trees with lighted lamps on them (दीपवृक्षैश् च सौवर्णैः); with different kinds of flags with bells hanging on them; it resounded with songs of men and women; the mountain became attractive to look at like Meru with hosts of sages on it (अतीव प्रेक्षनीयो ऽभून् मेरुर् मुनिगणैर् इव); many shops were set up for the festival which offered diverse kinds of food and wines; these were also freely given to poor, blind and miserable (सुरामैरेयमिश्रेण भक्ष्य-भोज्येन चैव ह । दीनान्धकृपणादिभ्यो दीयमानेन चानिशम्); there were holy lodgings set up for the meritorious people (पुण्यावसथवान् वीर पुण्यकृद्भिर् निषे-वितः); the mountain, full of houses meant for Vṛṣṇi heroes, appeared like the place of gods (स नगो वेश्मसंकीर्णो देवलोक इवाबभौ); due to the presence of Kṛṣṇa the mountain gave the appearance of the residence of Śakra (Indra) (शक्रसद्मप्रतीकाशो बभूव स हि शैलराट्) 14. 58. 4-14; the decorating of the mountain for its festival also described at another place: the Vṛṣṇis and the Andhakas gave gifts by thousands to Brāhmaṇas; the countryside around the mountain was decorated by palatial buildings shining with jewels and by trees holding the lamps; the players on musical instruments played on instruments, the dancers danced, and the singers sang; Vṛṣṇi princes, adorned, moved everywhere in their golden conveyances; the citizens also moved in thousands, with wives and retinue (सदाराः सानुयात्राश् च), either on foot or in vehicles 1. 211. 1-6. C. Epic events: (1) Kṛṣṇa went to Prabhāsa to meet Arjuna during the term of the latter's exile 1. 210. 4; from Prabhāsa the two went to Raivataka where they spent a night before going to Dvārakā; the mountain was deco-rated at the instance of Kṛṣṇa; Arjuna took food there and, in the company of Kṛṣṇa, saw the performances of actors and dancers (दृष्टवान् नटनर्तकान्) 1. 210. 8-10; Arjuna rested there on a decorated bed and, next morning, left Raivataka for Dvārakā 1. 210. 11-15; (2) After some days a great festival of the mountain was held by the Vṛṣṇis and the Andhakas for which the mountain Raivataka was decorated 1. 211. 1-2; all the important Yādavas like Ugrasena, Balarāma, Akrūra, Sātyaki, Kṛtavarman, Pradyumna, Sāmba, also Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna, participated in it; there Arjuna saw Subhadrā and fell in love with her 1. 211. 7-15; (3) On another occasion when Arjuna came to know that Subhadrā had gone to worship Raivataka he, with the consent of Kṛṣṇa, started for it 1. 212. 1-2; Subhadrā worshipp-ed the mountain Raivata and all the deities there and received blessings of the Brāhmaṇas; after making a प्रदक्षिणा of the mountain (ब्राह्मणान् स्वस्ति वाच्य च । प्रदक्षिणं गिरिं कृत्वा) she started to return to Dvārakā 1. 212. 6-7. D. Other events: (1) When the Mādhavas (Yādavas) left Mathurā to settle down at Kuśasthalī (Dvārakā) they were delighted to see the (Raivata) mountain 2. 13. 52; (2) When the Bhoja princes were sporting on the mountain Raivataka, Śiśupāla attacked them; he slew and captured them all (हत्वा बद्ध्वा च तान् सर्वान्) and returned to his town 2. 42. 8.

Raivata2, Raivataka2 m.: Name of a mountain of the Śākadvīpa. One of the seven mountains of the Śāka-dvīpa; described as very high (उच्चैर्गिरि) 6. 12. 16; all the seven mountains of this Dvīpa are said to be adorned with jewels (मणि-भूषिताः) and are mines of precious stones (रत्नाकराः) 6. 12. 13; the extent in योजनस् of these mountains is double the preceding one (तेषां योजनविष्कम्भो द्विगुणः प्र-विभागशः) 6. 12. 22; it is characterized by the the नक्षत्र Revatī in the sky (this explains the name of the mountain); that was the permanently established ordainment of Pitāmaha (Brahmadeva) (उच्चैर्गिरी रैव-तको यत्र नित्यं प्रतिष्ठितः । रेवती दिवि नक्षत्रम् पितामहकृतो विधिः) 6. 12. 16 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 11. 18: रेवती ज्योतिर्-मण्डलरूपेण दिवि विभ्रम्यमाणापि दिव्-येन रूपेणात्रापि वर्तते एवं विधिर् मर्यादा पितामहेन कृता); the Varṣa rela-ted to the mountain Raivata is Kaumāra 6. 12. 24.
रोहितकारण्य: Rohitakāraṇya nt.: Name of a forest. Mentioned among the places to which the army of the Kauravas spread out as it could not to be accommodated in Hāstinapura (न हास्तिनपुरे राजन्न् अवकाशो ऽभवत् तदा  … एष देशः सुवीस्तीर्णः … बभूव कौर-वेयाणां बलेन सुसमाकुलः 5. 19. 28, 31) 5. 19. 29.
रौप्या: Raupyā f.: Name of a river (?). Pointed out by Lomaśa to Yudhiṣṭhira; the highly illustrious son of Ārcīka who roamed on the earth with his Yogic powers withdrew (?) in the river Raupyā (एतद् आर्चीकपुत्रष्य योगैर् विचरतो महीम् । अपसर्पणं महीपाल रौप्यायाम् अमित-उजसः ॥ ) 3. 129. 7 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 3. 129. 7: रूप्यवत् श्वेतवर्णायां स्थल्यां नद्यां वा).
राजपुर: Rājapura1 nt.: Name of a town. A. Location: In the Kaliṅga country (कलिङ्गविषये … राजपुरं नाम नग-रम्) 12. 4. 2-3. B. Description: Wealthy (श्रीमन्त्) 12. 4. 3. C. Epic event: Citrāṅ-gada ruled this country; when the स्वयं-वर of the daughter of Citrāṅgada was held it was attended by Duryodhana, Karṇa and many other kings 12. 4. 3-4.

Rājapura2 nt. Name of a town. Located in the Kamboja country; while referring to the exploits of Karṇa, Bhīṣma said that he went to Rājapura and killed the Kāmboja warriors (कर्ण राजपुरं गत्वा काम्बोजा निहतास् त्वया) 7. 4. 4.
राजाश्रम: Rājāśrama m.: Name (?) of the her-mitage of a king. The hermitage was specially created by king Lomapāda of the Aṅgas (3. 110. 19) on the bank of the river to receive Ṛśyaśṛṅga when he was brought to Campā; the आश्रम was indeed a charming forest (तीराद् उपादाय तथैव चक्रे राजाश्रमं नाम वनं विचित्रम्) 3. 113. 9 (or, this to be read as राजा आश्रमं चक्रे and नाम to be treated as ind.).
रामस्य: Rāmasya āśramaḥ m.: The आश्रम established by Rāma. A. Location: On the river Godāvarī in the Daṇḍakāraṇya (दण्डकारण्यम् आश्रि-तः । नदीं गोदावरीं रम्याम् आश्रित्य न्य-वशत् तदा) 3. 261. 40. B. Rāmāyaṇa events: (1) Rāvaṇa abducted Sītā from (Rāma's) आश्रम (जानकी … हृता … आश्र-माद् राक्षसेन्द्रेण) 3. 258. 1-2; (2) Mārīca followed Rāvaṇa to the आश्रम of Rāma (ततस् तस्याश्रमं गत्वा रामस्य) 3. 262. 14; (3) Sītā refused to go with Rāvaṇa and again entered the आश्रम (इति सा तं समा-भाष्य प्रविवेशाश्रमं पुनः) 3. 262. 39; (4) After killing Mārīca, Rāma, anxious about Sītā who was left alone in the forest, hastened to his आश्रम (रामो ऽभ्यपतद् आश्रमम्) 3. 263. 15; (5) When Rāma reached the आश्रम he found that the grass-seats and pots there were broken, the jars were destroyed, the precincts of the आश्रम were empty, and a herd of jackals had occupied it (ततो दृष्ट्वाश्र-मपदम् व्यपविद्धबृसीघटम् । विध्व-स्तकलशं शून्यं गोमायुबलसेवितम् ॥ ) 3. 263. 22; (6) When Rāma and Lakṣ-maṇa knew about the abduction of Sītā, they left the आश्रम in search of her and went to the south of Daṇḍakāraṇya (वै-देहीहरणार्दितौ । जग्मतुर् दण्डकार-ण्यं दक्षिणेन परंतपौ) 3. 263. 23.
रुक्मिण्या: Rukmiṇyā āśramaḥ m.: Name of an आश्रम। The आश्रम was near the lake where कुश grass grew and where there were lotuses of the type of कुशेशय; Rukmiṇī found peace there (ह्रदश् च कुशवान् एष यत्र पद्मं कुशेशयम् । आशृअमश् चैव रुक्-मिण्या यत्राशाम्यद् अकोपना ॥ ) 3. 130. 15.
रुद्रस्य: Rudrasya āyatanam nt.: Name of the holy resort (temple ?) of Rudra along with his गण (रुद्रस्य सगणस्य)) 3. 118. 12. A. Location: In a forest, not very far from the sea and the तीर्थ called Śūrpāraka (शूर्पारकं ददर्श ॥ तत्रोदधेः कं-चिद् अतीत्य देशम् … वनम् आससाद) 3. 118. 8-9; (स तत्र … रुद्रस्य राजन् सगणस्य चैव … आयतनानि तेषां ददर्श) 3. 118. 10, 12, 13. For B. Description and C. Epic event see Bhagasya āyatanam.
रैभ्याश्रम: Raibhyāśrama m.: Name of the आश्रम of Raibhya. A. Description: Holy (पुण्य) 3. 137. 2; 3. 139. 24; splendid (श्रीमन्त्) 3. 135. 9; adorned by flowering trees (पुष्पितद्रुम-भूषित) 3. 137. 2; having trees with flowers and fruits at all times (सदापुष्पफलद्रुम) 3. 139. 24. B. Holiness: One who lives in Raibhyāśrama is freed of all sins (सर्वपा-पैः प्रमोक्ष्यसे) 3. 139. 24. C. Epic event: The आश्रम was shown by Lomaśa to Yudhiṣṭhira; the incidents related with the आश्रम were told by Lomaśa to him 3. 135. 9-3. 139. 23. D. Past event: Yavakrī(ta), son of Bharadvāja, once while wandering reached the precincts of the आश्रम of Raibhya (जगाम … रैभ्याश्रमपदं प्रति) 3. 137. 1; Yava-krī saw in the आश्रम the daughter-in-law of Raibhya 3. 137. 2; when Raibhya re-turned to his आश्रम, she told him what Yavakrī had asked of her 3. 137. 5, 7; the Rākṣasa after killing Yavakrīta returned to Raibhya (in his आश्रम) 3. 137. 20; the sage Yavakrīta perished at the आश्रम of Raibhya (एष रैभ्याश्रमः … भारद्वाजो यत्र कविर् यवक्रीतो व्यनश्यत) 3. 135. 9; when Arvāvasu and Parāvasu, the two sons of Raibhya, went with king Bṛhaddyumna to officiate at his sacrifice, Raibhya and the wife of Parāvasu remained behind in the आश्रम 3. 139. 3.
रोमा: Romā f.: Name of a city. It lay outside the Bhāratavarṣa; Saha-deva, in his expedition to the south of Indra-prastha (प्रययौ दक्षिणां दिशम् 2. 28. 1; दक्षिणाभिमुखो युयौ 2. 28. 8; प्रायाद् … दक्षिणां दिशम् 2. 28. 37) before the Rājasūya subjugated it just by sending messengers and made the people pay tribute (दूतैर् एव वशे चक्रे करं चैनान् अदा-पयत्) 2. 28. 49 (identified with Rome; cf. Edgerton JAOS 58. 262 ff. and his note on 2. 28. 49, Vol. 2, p. 502).
रोहीतक: Rohītaka nt.: Name of a city. A. Identification: According to Nī., however, a mountain (Bom. Ed. 2. 32. 5 रोहीतकं गिरिम्). B. Location: Situated to the west of Khāṇḍavaprastha (निर्याय खाण्डवप्रस्थात् प्रतीचीम् अभितो दिशम् 2. 29. 2). C. Description: Delightful (रम्य), wealthy (बहुधन), full of cows, horses, wealth and grain (गवाश्वधनधान्यवन्त्), dear to Kārtikeya (कार्तिकेयस्य दयितम्) 2. 29. 4. D. Epic event: Nakula in his expendition to the west before the Rājasūya invaded it and there was a great battle with heroic Mattamayūrakas (तत्र युद्धं महद् वृत्तं शूरैर् मत्तमयूरकैः) 2. 29. 5 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 32. 5: मत्त-मयूरसंज्ञैः क्षत्रियैः).
रथाकार: Rathākāra nt (sg.): Name of a Varṣa of the Kuśadvīpa in the north. A. Location: To the north of the Jambudvīpa (उत्तरेषु तु कौरव्य द्वीपेषु) 6. 13. 1; listed third in the collection of the Varṣas of the Kuśadvīpa (तृतीयं वै रथाकारं … सप्तैते वर्षपुञ्जकाः) 6. 13. 12-13. B. Characteristic: For the characteristic which is common to all the Varṣas see Audbhida.
रथोरग: Rathoraga m. (pl.): Name of a people (?) Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (वातजामरथो-रगाः) 6. 10. 53 (It is not clear how the compound is to be understood). [See Uraga, Vātajāma]
रमठ: Ramaṭha m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Location: To the west of the Khāṇḍavaprastha (see Epic event No. 1 below). B. Description: Fierce (उग्र) and doing cruel deeds (क्रूरकर्मन्) 8. 51. 18; they lived in countries but behaved like Dasyus (सर्वे विषयवासिनः । … सर्वे ते दस्युजीविनः) 12. 65. 15. C. Epic events: (1) Nakula in his expedition to the west before the Rājasūya (निर्याय खाण्डवप्रस्थात् प्रतीचीम् अभितो दिशम् 2. 29. 2; 2. 23. 10) subjugated Ramaṭhas (रमठान् … वशे चक्रे) 2. 29. 11: they attended the Rājasūya and acted as ser-vants in the sacrifice (यज्ञे ते परिवेष-कान्) 3. 48. 21-22; (2) Mentioned by Kṛṣṇa among those who had joined the Kuru army for the sake of Duryodhana; on one except Arjuna could defeat them (रमठतङ्गणाः । एते सुयोधनस्यार्थे संरब्धाः कुरुभिः सह । न शक्या युधि निर्जेतुम् त्वदन्येन परंतप ॥ ) 8. 51. 18, 20. D. Past event: King Māndhātṛ once asked Indra how people like Rama-ṭhas could be made to follow धर्म and how they could be controlled by kings like him (कथं धर्मं चरेयुस् ते … । मद्विधैश् च कथं स्थाप्याः) 12. 65. 15; Indra thereupon narrated to Māndhātṛ the duties of Dasyus 12. 65. 17-22.
रमणक: Ramaṇaka nt. (sg.): Name of a Varṣa of the Jambudvīpa. A. Location: It lay to the south of the Śveta mountain and to the north of the Nīla mountain 6. 9. 2. B. Description of the people: They were fair and born in the noble family, very pleasing to look at and given to pleasures (of love ?): their minds were always cheerful and they lived for ten thousand and fifteen hundred years (शुक्ला-भिजनसंपन्नाः सर्वे सुप्रियदर्शनाः । रतिप्रधानाश् च तथा जायन्ते तत्र मान-वाः ॥ दश वर्षसहस्राणि शतानि दश पञ्च च । जीवन्ति ते महाराज नित्यं मुदितमानसाः ॥ ) 6. 9. 3-4.
रमणीयक: Ramaṇīyaka nt. (sg.): Name of an island. A. Location: Situated in an isolated place in the bay of an ocean (समुद्र-कुक्षाव् एकान्ते) 1. 21. 4; (सागराम्बु-परीक्षिप्तम्) 1. 23. 1. B. Characteristic: It was the place where Nāgas lived (नागा-नाम् आलयं) 1. 21. 4. C. Description: very beautiful (सुरम्य) 1. 21. 4; made resonant by a large number of birds (पक्षि-संघनिनादित); a forest in Ramaṇīyaka was delightful to mind, holy and loved by Gandharvas and Apsarases; it was pleasing because it was full of sounds made by different kinds of birds (मनःसंहर्ष-णं पुण्यं गन्धर्वाप्सरसां प्रियम् । नानापक्षिरुतं रम्यं … ॥ ) 1. 23. 5; for the detailed description of the forest-its trees, mansions (भवनैर् आवृतं), lakes, breezes, and flowers see 1. 23. 2-5 ab. D. Past event: As asked by Kadrū, Vinatā took her, and Garuḍa the serpents to the island Ramaṇīyaka; on reaching the forest on the island the serpents merrily spent their time there (1. 21. 4-5; 1. 23. 6).
रम्यकागण: Ramyakāgaṇa m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (राजिका रम्यका-गणाः) 6. 10. 51.
राजिक: Rājika m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas) of Bhārata-varṣa; (राजिका रम्यकागणाः) (for cita-tions and references see the preceding entry Ramyakāgaṇa).
रोमन्: Roman m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जनपदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (रोमाणः कुश-बिन्दवः) 6. 10. 54; (for other references see Ramyakāgaṇa). [On the resemblance of the name, probably accidental, with Romans (inhabitants of Rome) see the Editor's note on this stanza in the Critical edition Vol. VII. p. 763. 2].
रोमश: Romaśa m. (pl.): Name of a people. Mentioned by Duryodhana along with Śakas, Tukhāras and others who brought as tribute for the Rājasūya an अर्बुद of horses of high breed and going long distances and also a पद्म of gold to be counted by crores; even then they were stopped at the gate and were not allowed to enter ( … रोमशाः … । महाग-मान् दूरगमान् गणितान् अर्बुदं हयान् ॥ कोटिशश् चैव बहुशः सुवर्णं पद्म-संमितम् । बलिम् आदाय विविधं द्वारि तिष्ठन्ति वारिताः ॥ ) 2. 47. 26-27 (Are these Romans ? See Romā Cul. Ind. Vol. II. p. 559 and Roman above).
